# Question: generator-shortcuts

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that
> fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees
> with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed
> generator emits such cases.

## Answer

The strongest plausible rival I found is **rotations only**: take the color-8
stencil and recolor color-3 copies matching one of its four rotations, but never
consider reflected copies. It fits **4/4 canonical training demonstrations**.
It is stronger and more task-specific than simple position, count, or palette
shortcuts because it performs the intended operation on every orientation shown
in training while omitting exactly the unshown branch of the dihedral group.

On this input, the selected Racket output matches the canonical recorded output.
The rotations-only rival leaves four cells as color 3 that the intended rule
changes to color 8:

| zero-based cell | rival | intended |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| (13,2) | 3 | 8 |
| (13,3) | 3 | 8 |
| (14,3) | 3 | 8 |
| (14,4) | 3 | 8 |

I checked this three ways:

1. `checks/shortcut-canonical/racket.json` was produced through the public
   `arcpuzzles apply` command against selected authority and equals the canonical
   expected output.
2. The independent geometry oracle in
   `repo/generators/195dfcc5b541/workspace/reference_probe.py` reproduces all
   five canonical pairs; the rotations-only variant reproduces the four training
   pairs but not this test pair.
3. The task test `test_real_racket_authority_matches_independent_geometry_oracle`
   compares selected Racket with the independent oracle on all five canonical
   inputs plus 24 generated inputs. The complete exact counterexample and hashes
   are in `checks/shortcut-canonical/counterexample.json`.

The repaired generator **emits such cases on every draw**, not merely with a
small probability. It uses a chiral stencil and constructively plants at least
one rotation plus one reflection-only color-3 copy. The retained declaration-aware
probe found a rotations-only disagreement on **120/120 generated inputs** across
all bands (`checks/shortcut-probe.json`). The larger three-demo census found no
surviving rotations-only ambiguity in **300/300 production lessons** or any of
**1,200/1,200 query rotations** (`checks/lesson-census-final.json`). These finite
checks establish coverage against this declared rival, not universal uniqueness
against every possible program.
